paper_information.title: Biology of Solanum tuberosum (POTATO)
paper_information.journal_or_source: Series of Crop Specific Biology Documents, Phase II Capacity Building Project on Biosafety, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India & Central Potato Research Institute, Shimla
paper_information.abstract_summary: This document provides comprehensive baseline biological information on potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) including taxonomy, origin, distribution in India, morphology, reproductive biology, ecology, human health considerations, cultivation practices, insect pests, and major diseases to serve as a credible source of information for biosafety assessment of genetically modified plants.
paper_information.research_objective: To compile biological baseline information on potato as a reference for risk assessment of genetically modified plants.
important_findings: Potato is the third most important non-grain food crop globally.
In India, potato is grown in 1.99 million ha across 26 states, with 90% coming from the Indo-Gangetic plains.
Major constraints include late blight, bacterial wilt, and various viral and insect pests.
The potato genome sequence has been completed by the Potato Genome Sequencing Consortium.

early_symptoms: Water-soaked irregular pale green lesions mostly near tip and margins of leaves
advanced_symptoms: Rapidly grow into large brown to purplish black necrotic spots
A white mildew consisting of sporangia and spores of the pathogen can be seen on the lower surface of infected leaves around the edges of necrotic lesions

field_identification: Water-soaked irregular pale green lesions turning into brown/purplish-black necrotic spots with white mildew on the underside

research_findings: Highly regulated potato late blight resistance genes R1, R2, RB, R3a, Rpi-blb2, and Rpi-vnt1.1 were present in the potato genome assembly.

general: Small, round, oval or angular, dark brown to black, dry and papery necrotic spots on leaves limited by leaf veins
Concentric rings of raised and depressed tissue within the leaf spot give it a bull's eye or target board appearance
Leaf tissues around spots often become chlorotic and yellow
Leaf spots may coalesce and the field may get severely blighted

field_identification: Concentric rings of raised and depressed tissue on leaf spots giving a bull's eye or target board appearance

general: Black irregular lumpy encrustations of fungal sclerotia on potato tubers
Cracking, malformation, pitting, and stem end necrosis on tubers
Stem canker and formation of aerial tubers on stems in disease-affected plants

field_identification: Black irregular lumpy encrustations on potato tubers

general: Small brown lesions on the surface of affected tubers
Lesions subsequently enlarge, appear dark, sunken, and wrinkled, producing white, pink, or blue pustules
In later stages a cavity develops in the centre of the concentric ring and whitish, pinkish or dark brown growth of fungal mycelium may become visible

field_identification: Small brown lesions on tubers turning dark, sunken, and wrinkled with white, pink, or blue pustules

general: Purplish brown sunken lesions on potato tubers which later turn to scab like lesions
Lesions are round, raised, filled with powdery mass of spores and surrounded by ruptured remains of epidermal layers

field_identification: Round, raised scab-like lesions filled with a powdery mass of spores and surrounded by ruptured epidermis
differential_diagnosis: Unlike common scab, lesions of powdery scab are round, raised, filled with powdery mass of spores and surrounded by ruptured remains of epidermal layers.

general: Symptoms on tubers develop around eyes, lenticels and stolon end where a dark light grey, soft, water-soaked lesion develops on the surface
Subsequently, lesions become filled with black mycelium and sclerotia of the pathogen
Lesions may shrink and develop symptoms similar to dry rots under low moisture conditions

field_identification: Dark light grey, soft, water-soaked lesions around eyes, lenticels, and stolon ends filled with black mycelium and sclerotia

general: Slight wilting of youngest leaves during hot sunny days followed by drooping due to loss of turgidity and total unrecoverable wilt
Cross-sections of stems show vascular discolouration
Transversely cut tubers show water-soaked brown circles in vascular tissues where dirty white sticky drops appear in 2-3 minutes
In advanced stages of wilt, bacterial mass may ooze out from eyes
early_symptoms: Slight wilting of youngest leaves during hot sunny days
advanced_symptoms: Total unrecoverable wilt, vascular discolouration, bacterial ooze from vascular rings and tuber eyes

field_identification: Wilting of young leaves, vascular discolouration of stem, and confirming by placing stem cut sections in clear water to observe bacterial streaming
diagnostic_methods: Placing stem cut sections in clear water to observe bacterial streaming
differential_diagnosis: Bacterial wilt in field can be distinguished from fungal wilts by placing the stem cut sections in clear water to observe bacterial streaming.

general: Small reddish or brownish spots on the surface of potato tubers during juvenile period
Lesions become corky due to elongation and division of invaded cells
Symptoms range from a few superficial or raised brown spots on the skin to dark pits extending several millimetres into the tuber resulting in reduced market value
early_symptoms: Small reddish or brownish spots on the surface of potato tubers during juvenile period
advanced_symptoms: Corky lesions ranging from superficial raised brown spots to dark pits extending several millimeters into the tuber

field_identification: Corky lesions, raised brown spots, or deep dark pits on potato tubers

general: Initially a small area of tuber tissue around lenticels or stolon attachment point becomes water-soaked and develops soft lesions
Under high humidity, lesions enlarge and spread; decaying tissue becomes slimy with foul smell and brown liquid ooze
Black leg symptoms in cooler regions: affected haulms become black at collar region just above ground
On stem and petioles, lesions enlarge into stripes, turn black, and cause soft rot and toppling of stem and leaves
early_symptoms: Small water-soaked area around lenticels or stolon attachment on tubers
advanced_symptoms: Slimy decay with foul smell, black collar region, toppling of stems and leaves

field_identification: Water-soaked soft lesions on tubers with foul-smelling slime, black lesions on stems/collars

general: Affected plants are stunted with mild or severe mosaic and veinal necrosis
Original strain PVYO causes mosaic, necrotic spots, mild rugosity, and drying of leaves

field_identification: Stunted plants with mosaic, veinal necrosis, and rugosity

general: Mild mosaic symptoms somewhat similar to PVX
Mottles appear on the veins and infected leaves look shiny
Infected plants show an open habit
Severe leaf crinkle may be produced in combination with PVX

field_identification: Mild mosaic with mottles on veins and shiny leaves with an open plant habit
differential_diagnosis: Unlike PVX, mottles caused by PVA appear on the veins and infected leaves look shiny.

general: Plants infected with PVX often remain symptomless
When symptoms are expressed, pattern of light and dark green on leaflets with lighter, small, irregular blotches between veins
Can interact with PVY and PVA to cause more severe symptoms such as rugose mosaic (PVX+PVY) and crinkle mosaic (PVX+PVA)

field_identification: Often symptomless or showing light and dark green patterns with irregular blotches between veins

general: Causes mottle, mosaic, crinkling, rolling (spoon-shaped leaves) of leaves and stunting of shoots

field_identification: Leaf rolling (spoon-shaped leaves), mottle, mosaic, crinkling, and shoot stunting

general: Primary symptoms confined to top young leaves which stand upright, roll, and turn slightly pale

Secondary symptoms (from infected seed tubers) prominent in older leaves: plants have characteristic pale, dwarfed, and upright appearance with rolling of lower leaves that turn yellow, brittle, and leathery
Reddish or purple discolouration on margins and underside of leaves in some cultivars
early_symptoms: Top young leaves stand upright, roll, and turn slightly pale
advanced_symptoms: Pale, dwarfed, upright appearance, rolling of lower leaves, yellowing, brittleness, leathery texture, marginal reddish/purple discoloration

field_identification: Uprigth pale appearance, rolling of lower leaves turning yellow, brittle, and leathery

general: Symptomless on majority of potato cultivars
Occasional mild leaf symptoms of rugosity, vein deepening, and bronzing
Rugosity, mosaic, stunting, bronzing, vein deepening, early drop of leaves, and fine necrotic spots on lower leaves reported occasionally in some cultivars

field_identification: Usually symptomless or occasional mild rugosity, vein deepening, and bronzing

disease_development_and_spread: Transmitted mainly by contact and by aphids

diseases.causal_agent: Tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus-potato (ToLCNDV-potato)

general: Affected plants show curling / crinkling of apical leaves with a conspicuous mosaic symptom
In case of seed-borne infection, entire plant shows leaf distortion with mosaic accompanied with severe stunting
Symptoms are very severe and easily identified when virus concentration is very high
advanced_symptoms: Curling/crinkling of apical leaves, mosaic, severe stunting of the plant

field_identification: Curling and crinkling of apical leaves with mosaic and severe plant stunting

paper_level_notes: The document contains detailed sections on potato botany, taxonomy, cultivation zones in India, insect pests, nematodes, fungal diseases, bacterial diseases, viral diseases, breeding objectives, and biotechnological interventions.
